name: Cahokia
place: Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site, Illinois
blurb: The largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, around 1050–1350 CE. Monks Mound is the biggest earthwork in the Americas north of Mexico.
about: From about 1050 to 1350 CE, Cahokia was the largest city north of Mexico, home at its peak to perhaps 10,000 to 15,000 people. Monks Mound is about 30 m tall and covers 14 acres, all of it carried up by hand in baskets of earth, with a large building once on top. Around it were more than a hundred other mounds, a great plaza, and 'Woodhenge,' rings of tall posts used to track the sun. It's a state historic site and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, just across the Mississippi from St. Louis.
